fixes.explanation: Oh, friend, that one's a trap, and I walked right up to it too. Paul says the opposite: "It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again…" (Philippians 3:1). He isn't calling it a chore. And he adds that it is "…a safeguard for you."

You've got it, baker. Paul says, "It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again…" (Philippians 3:1). Nobody's rolling their eyes at the pen here. He says it's no trouble, and he calls it a safeguard for them.

Nope, no scolding in this line, friend. Paul isn't pointing a finger and saying "I told you so." He says writing the same things again "…is a safeguard for you." (Philippians 3:1). That's a protection, not a telling-off.

Moses was Israel's leader who received the law (Exodus 24:12), so I get the guess, friend. But Paul never names Moses in this verse. He says they "…glory in Christ Jesus…" (Philippians 3:3). That's where all the glory goes.

You've got it, baker. Paul counts all things as loss compared to "…the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord…" (Philippians 3:8). Nothing else comes close to that. Paul even says he has lost all things for Him.

Good guess, friend, since Paul said he was "faultless" as to righteousness in the law (Philippians 3:6). But he counts even that as loss for the sake of Christ (Philippians 3:7). What outshines it is "…the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord…" (Philippians 3:8).

I can see why the temple came to mind, friend, since it was the place of worship in Jerusalem (1 Kings 8:10-11). But Paul doesn't say a word about it in this verse. He sets righteousness from the law against righteousness "…through faith in Christ…" (Philippians 3:9).

Friend, Paul doesn't split it up. He writes, "I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings…" (Philippians 3:10). He wants both, not one without the other. That makes this statement False.

Rest sounds nice, friend, but that's not what Paul says here. He wants "…to attain to the resurrection from the dead." (Philippians 3:11). That's the goal he names. Rest from his work isn't in the verse.
